paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : MMLU confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy for three distinct models, displaying accuracy values alongside confidence scores. The x-axis represents Initial Confidence, spanning a linear scale from 0.88 to 1.00 with tick marks incrementing by 0.01. The y-axis represents Accuracy, ranging from 0.86 to 1.00 with tick marks incrementing by 0.10. A solid blue line, denoted by "Final Accuracy," consistently displays a value near 0.98 throughout the x-axis, with a minimum value of approximately 0.97 at x = 0.97 and a maximum of 0.98 at x = 0.99. A dashed orange line, representing Δ Accuracy, begins at approximately 0.88 at x = 0.88 and decreases to around 0.86 at x = 0.99. A green line, labeled as Initial Accuracy, starts at approximately 0.86 at x = 0.88 and steadily declines to a value of 0.78 at x = 0.99. A dotted green line, representing the “Initial Accuracy” starts at approximately 0.86 at x = 0.88 and decreases to a value of 0.78 at x = 0.99.
